If you've been searching for a capable, iconic off-roader with a stick shift and serious trail credentials, this 2007 Toyota FJ Cruiser for sale at Siry Motors in San Diego, CA is exactly what you've been looking for. Silver in finish, equipped with a 4.0-liter V6, a 6-speed manual transmission, and full 4WD, this FJ Cruiser is a rare combination of retro style, mechanical simplicity, and genuine off-road capability and it's available now in San Diego County.

===== About This 2007 Toyota FJ Cruiser =====

At 107,673 miles, this 2007 FJ Cruiser sits comfortably in the middle of its usable life. Toyota's 4.0-liter V6 the same engine found in the Tacoma and 4Runner is well-documented to run well past 200,000 miles with basic maintenance, meaning this truck has plenty of life left in it. The silver exterior gives it a clean, understated look that pairs well with the FJ's boxy, retro-inspired body design. If you've been hunting for a used Toyota FJ Cruiser in San Diego County, this one checks the boxes: honest miles, a desirable drivetrain, and a body style that simply doesn't age.

===== 2007 Toyota FJ Cruiser Performance and Engine =====

==== 4.0-Liter V6 and 6-Speed Manual ====

The 1GR-FE 4.0-liter V6 under the hood produces 239 horsepower and 278 lb-ft of torque numbers that were genuinely impressive for a mid-2000s truck-based SUV and remain competitive today. Paired with the 6-speed manual transmission, this configuration is the enthusiast's choice. Manual FJ Cruisers are significantly rarer than their automatic counterparts, making this vehicle a standout on the used market. The manual gearbox gives you precise control on technical terrain, better engine braking on descents, and a more engaging driving experience on the highway.

The 4WD system uses a part-time layout with a locking center differential, giving you solid traction management whether you're navigating the backcountry of Anza-Borrego, crawling through the Cuyamaca Mountains, or just commuting around San Diego. Ground clearance is generous at 9.6 inches, and the approach and departure angles are trail-ready from the factory.

===== Toyota FJ Cruiser Features and Interior =====

==== Built for Function, Not Frills ====

The FJ Cruiser's interior design mirrors its purpose: durable, washable surfaces, a tall greenhouse with great outward visibility, and a layout built to be used hard. The rear suicide-style doors open wide for cargo or passenger access, and the flat rear floor makes it easy to load gear for weekend trips. Standard features on 2007 FJ Cruisers include air conditioning, power windows and locks, a multi-information display, and Toyota's intuitive audio system. The seating is supportive on long drives, and the upright windshield gives the cabin a spacious, open feel that's unique among SUVs of this era.

===== Toyota FJ Cruiser Reliability and Ownership =====

==== One of Toyota's Most Durable Platforms ====

The FJ Cruiser has developed a devoted following precisely because it's so dependable. Built on the same platform as the 4Runner and sharing mechanicals with the Land Cruiser Prado, this SUV benefits from decades of proven off-road engineering. Owners consistently report that the 1GR-FE V6 requires little beyond oil changes and spark plugs to keep running strong. Known issues on early FJs are minor rear differential breather tube maintenance on water crossings, and keeping up with transfer case fluid changes but nothing that approaches a major mechanical concern. The FJ Cruiser was discontinued after 2014, and values have held remarkably well in the resale market as demand continues to outpace supply. Buying one today, even with six-figure miles, is widely regarded as a smart long-term investment in the enthusiast community.
